newsitem.title: FINLAND: Silja sees no impact of Sea Wind incident.
newsitem.headline: Silja sees no impact of Sea Wind incident.

text.p: Finnish passenger ferry operator Silja Oy Ab is confident that an accident involving its Sea Wind ferry off the coast of Sweden will have no impact on group business, Silja's CFO said on Wednesday.

"I don't believe this will have any impact of that kind," chief financial officer Henrik Osterberg told Reuters by telephone when asked whether the running aground of Sea Wind could hurt passenger figures and affect prospects for 1997.
The Sea Wind ferry, which belongs to Silja's SeaWind Line Oy Ab unit, ran aground off Stockholm early on Wednesday. All 107 passengers were evacuated safely.
"This incident itself will not affect people's willingness to travel," Osterberg said.

The minor accident was unlikely to awaken the sort of fears that emerged after the sinking of an Estonian passenger ferry in 1994 with the loss of 852 lives, which Baltic Sea ferry operators have said hurt passenger traffic, he said.
"Because nothing dramatic has occurred here (the Sea Wind accident), I don't think it will have that sort of effect."

The incident was unlikely to have any effect on Silja's 1997 earnings prospects, Osterberg said, referring to the group's 1996 report in which it said the positive trend in 1996 earnings would continue this year.
"We believe that in 1997 the whole group will achieve break-even, or make a slight profit," Osterberg said.
"I don't think this thing (the Sea Wind accident) will have any effect (on Silja's share price) because I don't think it will have any effect on earnings," he said.
Silja was untraded on the Helsinki bourse at 1130/0930 GMT on Wednesday after closing at 47.00 markka on Tuesday.
Sea Wind accounted for "a very small share" of Silja's total passenger volume and its expected absence from service during repairs would have no major impact on passenger figures, Osterberg said.
Silja would be able to serve Sea Wind passengers with other vessels it operates on the same Turku-Stockholm route, he added.
